section_summary: Section contains the tail of Japan's 1948 annual report on narcotics to the UN (laws, administration, seizures, drug control), forwarded by the UN Secretary-General in August 1949 with the text of Law No. 238. It then includes a Tokyo despatch of September 1949 on narcotics in Japan restituted to China, a note on Ryukyu estimates for dilaudide, and December 1949 telegrams on deleting a narcotics article from the Japanese peace treaty.

subfiles.about: Annual report on Japan's narcotic laws, administration, seizures, trade and control for 1948.
subfiles.summary: Describes Narcotic and Marihuana Control Laws and amendment, Narcotic Section staffing, enforcement statistics, Protocol of 1946 agreement, illicit traffic and seizure cases, prices, raw materials, manufacturers, licensees and prepared opium. Notes heroin smoking among foreign nationals.
subfiles.title: Japan annual report on narcotics for 1948

subfiles.about: UN cover for laws communicated under the 1931 Narcotic Drugs Convention, with State Department file stamps.
subfiles.summary: UN cover sheet with Department filing stamps.
subfiles.title: UN cover sheet for laws and regulations communicated under 1931 Convention

subfiles.about: Forwards text communicated by the United States Government under Article 21 of the 1931 Convention.
subfiles.summary: UN document header and note forwarding the U.S.-communicated text; page 270 is blank.
subfiles.title: Note by the Secretary-General, E/NR.1949/56
subfiles.to: Members of the United Nations and parties to the Convention

subfiles.about: Text adding Article 52(2) creating up to 250 armed Narcotic Agents, effective January 1, 1949.
subfiles.summary: Amends Narcotic Control Law to designate Narcotic Agents with judicial police powers, authority to carry small arms, and effective date.
subfiles.title: Law No. 238, Law for Partial Amendment to the Narcotic Control Law

subfiles.about: Reports information from Ely Brandes on opium and morphine in Japan restituted to the Chinese government by GHQ.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Brandes says China claimed opium and morphine identified as removed from China, held at three Japanese plants. Restitution was a paper transfer with GHQ keeping custody. Sale proceeds remain disputed; no samples released to Wu; no concern over illicit sale.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 674: Narcotics in Japan Restituted to China

subfiles.about: Requests entering 21 grams in the 1949 Ryukyu estimate form for dilaudide tablets imported at SCAP request.
subfiles.summary: Refers to July 26, 1948 note; SCAP asks quantity of 21 grams be entered for dilaudide tablets.
subfiles.title: Note to Permanent Central Board on dilaudide estimate for Ryukyus
subfiles.to: President of the Permanent Central Board, Bern

subfiles.about: Relays USPOLAD Tokyo recommendation to delete narcotics article from the Japanese peace treaty.
subfiles.summary: Proposes deleting or changing the narcotics article, since other countries might cite it as precedent; asks Anslinger's views.
subfiles.title: Telegram 1018 to Mexico City for Anslinger

subfiles.about: Anslinger expects UK, Canada and China to insist on the narcotics article and suggests rewording to a general principle.
subfiles.summary: Believes wording can be changed to state a principle acceptable to all; will return to Washington December 20 to propose wording.
subfiles.title: Telegram 1424 from Mexico City, Anslinger reply
